nodes.name: Biological soil crust
nodes.desc: A living skin of cyanobacteria, lichens and mosses on desert soil. It binds soil against erosion and some of its cyanobacteria fix nitrogen, but footsteps can break it up and recovery is very slow.

nodes.name: Indian ricegrass
nodes.desc: A bunchgrass of sandy desert soil, among the best-recorded grasses in the park area. Its seeds and foliage feed rodents and grazers.

nodes.name: Blackbrush
nodes.desc: A low, dense desert shrub of the Colorado Plateau, browsed by deer and bighorn sheep.

nodes.name: Utah juniper
nodes.desc: A drought-tolerant tree of the pinyon-juniper woodland on the mesas. Its foliage and berry-like cones feed deer and squirrels.

nodes.name: Pinyon pine
nodes.desc: A small pine whose large seeds are a key food for jays, squirrels and mice in the woodland.

nodes.name: Ord's kangaroo rat
nodes.desc: The most-recorded mammal in the park area. A nocturnal seed-eating rodent that is prey for foxes, coyotes and owls.

nodes.name: Deer mouse
nodes.desc: A small, nocturnal, omnivorous rodent, widespread and abundant, that eats seeds and insects and feeds many predators.

nodes.name: Rock squirrel
nodes.desc: A large ground squirrel of rocky canyon country that eats seeds, nuts and juniper berries.

nodes.name: Pinyon jay
nodes.desc: A social jay that feeds heavily on pinyon seeds and is well recorded in the park area.

nodes.name: Darkling beetles
nodes.desc: Ground beetles of desert country that feed on plant material and detritus and are common food for small predators.

nodes.name: Desert bighorn sheep
nodes.desc: A sure-footed grazer and browser of the canyon rims and cliffs, and a prey of mountain lions.

nodes.name: Mule deer
nodes.desc: A crepuscular browser that eats shrubs and grasses and feeds lions, coyotes and scavengers.

nodes.name: Northern grasshopper mouse
nodes.desc: A small carnivorous mouse that hunts insects such as beetles and sometimes other small rodents.

nodes.name: Gray fox
nodes.desc: An omnivorous canid of rocky, wooded canyons that takes mice, birds, and carrion.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: The most-recorded bird in the park area. An intelligent omnivore that scavenges carrion.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: A soaring scavenger that feeds on carcasses and cleans up dead animals across the canyons.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: A flexible, dawn-and-dusk predator of rodents and deer that also takes carrion.

nodes.name: Mountain lion
nodes.desc: A mostly nocturnal ambush predator of the canyons that hunts deer and bighorn sheep.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Powers both the crust and plants of an open, sunlit landscape.

nodes.name: Rain & snowmelt
nodes.desc: Scarce, irregular water drives plant growth and crust activity in this arid plateau.

nodes.name: Desert soil & nutrients
nodes.desc: Sandy, thin soil that holds nutrients plants draw on, topped by the crust.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and invertebrates that recycle dead plants and animals into the soil.
